note: Class-level security evidence (TASK-N1-O5). Thirteen components declare the same `url` boundary and cross it in the same two ways, so their threat model is one document and their corpus is one suite driven by shared fixture data. The capability-matrix generator resolves security evidence by the filename convention `{Component}.{kind}.{md,spec.ts}`, which cannot see either; the alternative was thirteen stub documents whose only content is a pointer, which is the box-ticking this matrix exists to expose. So the coverage is declared here and the generator checks both that the file exists and that the claim is about a real component. DzFileUpload is absent on purpose: it is the Tier D component and carries its own four per-component artifacts.

artifacts.why: One document, two threat models (navigation vs subresource) plus the payload boundary. Writing it fourteen times would hide the distinction that is the finding.

Every url declarer is bound to its own sink in boundary-bindings.ts and measured against the shared url-scheme fixtures. Since TASK-R2-O4 that includes DzQRCode: `securityBoundary` is a set, the component declares `['url', 'payload']`, and its `icon` sink — asserted here since TASK-N1-O5 as finding U3 — is now the evidence for a row the matrix asks for. The six navigation sinks assert the allowlist in packages/core/src/security/url-policy.ts; the eight subresource sinks assert `inert`, which is a property of `` and not of a policy.
Hostile content — markup injection and degenerate input — through each component's own label, alt, caption or fallback prop, plus the CSS-injection cases on DzQRCode's `color`.
